newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea may open airspace in early 97-IATA official.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea may open airspace in early 97-IATA official.

text.p: North Korea would be ready to open up its airspace for overflights by foreign carriers early this year, a senior official from the International Air Transport Association (IATA) said on Friday.
Pierre Jeanniot, director general of the Montreal-based organisation, told reporters North Korea's bitter political foe South Korea would not be excluded.

"Recent developments ... will soon make the use of (North Korea's) airspace a reality ... hopefully from early in 1997," he said. "All members, including Korean Air Lines (of South Korea), can fly over North Korea."
The two Koreas are technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not in a peace accord.

Seoul has gradually eased restrictions on contacts with North Koreans after Pyongyang issued a rare apology in December for infiltrating a Shark-class submarine that dropped 26 commandos on a Southern beach last September.
Jeanniot said some technical issues, including communications, were delaying Pyongyang's plan to open air routes for international aviation companies.
Potential new routes through the airspace of North Korea would cut flight times substantially between North America and Seoul and between other points in Asia, he said.
A saving on time and fuel, he said, would cut costs for carriers operating in the region by more than $125 million a year.
Jeanniot arrived in South Korea for a two-day visit to see the nation's aviation infrastructure, including construction of a new international airport on the western island of Yongjong.
